name: Torona
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.note: No phonology section; sole reference is Norton & Alaki 2016, WOCAL-7 proceedings pp.152-177 (Langaa).

sources.citation: Quint, Nicolas. 2020. Kordofanian. In Vossen & Dimmendaal (eds.), The Oxford Handbook of African Languages (halshs-03093501).
sources.note: Torona appears only as lexical items in comparative tables; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Smits, Heleen. 2017. A Grammar of Lumun: a Kordofanian language of Sudan. Utrecht: LOT (Leiden PhD).
sources.note: Torona mentioned only for history (community ceased to exist), classification (Lumun-Torona split) and a segmental remark from Norton & Kuku Alaki 2015; nothing on Torona prosody.

sources.citation: Norton, Russell & Thomas Kuku Alaki. 2015. The Talodi languages: a comparative-historical analysis. Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 11: 47-161. Entebbe: SIL-South Sudan.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a catalogue record only (no print holding to request from, no digital copy known)
sources.note: Nothing on stress (the word 'stress' occurs 0 times in the volume). Sec. 3.2.5 'Note on Length and Tone', p.107: 'We omit analysis of prosodic features for lack of data and for lack of functional load.. there is some evidence from Torona that variable compensatory lengthening has a rhythmic function (Norton & Alaki to appear).' Two tone levels reported family-wide; vowel length non-contrastive. Torona data = own 2012 elicitation from the last speaker. Fn.29 p.85: Lumun-Torona branch 'was not available' in Schadeberg 1981.

sources.citation: Voegelin, C. F. & F. M. Voegelin. 1964. Languages of the World: African Fascicle One. Anthropological Linguistics 6(5). (ERIC microfiche scan, archive.org micro_IA41153350_0260)
sources.note: Talodi branch sec. 1.7.3 (pp.197-198) is classification/population only ('torona, in a small settlement in Moro Hills'); the 'stress unit' passage (p.301) surfaced by full-text search concerns Berber. Nothing on Torona or Talodi stress.

sources.citation: archive.org full-text and metadata searches ('Torona' Talodi; 'Torona' stress syllable Nuba; Talodi stress Masakin Lumun; creator Schadeberg / title Kordofanian|Talodi), CrossRef query for the WOCAL-7 chapter.
sources.note: Hits are Wikipedia PDF dumps, Murdock 1959, Ethnologue editions, Mann & Dalby 1987, Voegelin 1964, Tucker & Bryan 1956 Handbook (borrow-only) -- classification lists only; no Torona phonology passage; no DOI registered for the 2016 chapter.

sources.citation: Norton, Russell & Thomas Kuku Alaki. 2016. Torona: a disappearing Talodi language of Sudan. In G. G. Atindogbe & E. F. Chibaka (eds.), Proceedings of the 7th World Congress of African Linguistics, Buea, 17-21 August 2012, pp. 152-177. Bamenda: Langaa RPCIG.

sources.note: The only first-hand description of Torona (2012 elicitation from the last proficient speaker); OPSL 11 p.107 cites it for a rhythmic function of compensatory lengthening in Torona, so it is the one place a stress/rhythm statement could exist. Glottolog tags it 'wordlist' (26 pp).
